s1.syndrome_frame: Acute orbital syndrome with pain, vision loss, and extraocular movement limitation
salient_findings: Diffuse limitation in extraocular movements in the left eye
Left-sided lacrimal sac abscess with postseptal fat stranding
key_facts: History of epiphora without prior dacryocystitis
Left-sided lacrimal sac abscess on CT
Acute injury to the entire orbital segment of the left optic nerve on MRI
Cultures isolated gram-positive cocci in chains, later identified as pan-susceptible Streptococcus pyogenes

raw.syndrome_frame: Acute orbital syndrome with pain, vision loss, and extraocular movement limitation
salient_findings: Diffuse limitation in extraocular movements in the left eye
Left-sided lacrimal sac abscess with postseptal fat stranding
key_facts: History of epiphora without prior dacryocystitis
Left-sided lacrimal sac abscess on CT
Acute injury to the entire orbital segment of the left optic nerve on MRI
Cultures isolated gram-positive cocci in chains, later identified as pan-susceptible Streptococcus pyogenes

shortlist.label: Lacrimal sac abscess
shortlist.why_kept: Imaging studies confirmed left-sided lacrimal sac abscess

shortlist.label: Orbital cellulitis
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation of orbital pain, edema, and hyperemia

shortlist.label: Orbital abscess
shortlist.why_kept: Follow-up CT showed increased abscess size with globe compression

shortlist.label: Cavernous sinus thrombosis
shortlist.why_kept: Diffuse limitation in extraocular movements and vision loss

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of epiphora, left orbital pain, and imaging studies showing a left-sided lacrimal sac abscess with postseptal fat stranding and globe compression are most consistent with a lacrimal sac abscess, which is a localized infection that can cause these symptoms and findings.

rejected.label: Orbital cellulitis
rejected.why: While the patient has signs of orbital inflammation, the presence of a discrete abscess on imaging suggests a more localized process than cellulitis alone.

rejected.label: Streptococcal orbital infection
rejected.why: The cultures did identify Streptococcus pyogenes, but this is more of a causative agent rather than a specific diagnosis for the patient's condition.

rejected.label: Orbital abscess
rejected.why: The imaging studies specifically identify the abscess as being in the lacrimal sac, making lacrimal sac abscess a more precise diagnosis.

rejected.label: Cavernous sinus thrombosis
rejected.why: There is no mention of findings suggestive of cavernous sinus thrombosis, such as bilateral orbital signs or specific imaging evidence of thrombosis in the cavernous sinuses.
